Compute a graph layout

Source: R/layout.R
cgraph_layout.Rd

Computes node coordinates for plot.cgraph().

Usage

cgraph_layout(
  x,
  method = NULL,
  direction = c("right", "down", "up", "left"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A graph created with cgraph(), of any class.

method

Character string specifying the layout method:

  • "sugiyama": layered/hierarchical layout, from the Sugiyama.jl package. Every edge is layered from its first to its second node (A --> B puts A before B), and any cycles are broken, so it works for every graph class.

  • "stress": stress majorization (Gansner, Koren and North, 2005), starting from classical multidimensional scaling. A good general-purpose choice - well-spaced and deterministic for a given graph.

  • "shell": nodes evenly spaced on a circle, in nodes() order.

  • "squaregrid": nodes on a square grid, row by row in nodes() order.

Defaults (NULL) to "sugiyama" when x was constructed (or reclass()ed) as a DAG, "stress" otherwise. This checks x's actual class, not its edge structure (see predicates) - a PDAG with only directed, acyclic edges still defaults to "stress".

direction

For "sugiyama", which way the layers flow: "right" (the default, as in CausalStructures.jl), "down", "up" or "left".

...

Ignored, so that plot.cgraph() can pass its ... through.

Value

A data.frame with columns name, x, and y.

See also

Other plotting: plot.cgraph(), plot_default_options(), plot_options()

Examples

if (julia_ready()) {
  dag <- cgraph(A %-->% B, B %-->% C)
  cgraph_layout(dag)
  cgraph_layout(dag, method = "stress")
}
#>   name            x             y
#> 1    A  1.00000e+00 -8.603189e-09
#> 2    B  5.85951e-17  1.720638e-08
#> 3    C -1.00000e+00 -8.603189e-09
